funding_amount: Up to $28,000 for training that is 1 year or less; up to $35,000 for programs more than 1 year and up to 2 years. Amount depends on individual needs and available funding.
eligibility: Applicant has been laid off and is not working.
Applicant has been laid off and is working a temporary job only to cover costs.
Applicant has not been laid off, but has been unemployed for 12 weeks or longer and is part of a low-income household.
Applicants receiving EI, Ontario Works, or ODSP may still apply.
Application is completed with support from an Employment Ontario service provider.
notes: The official page does not target exact NOC codes. Use this record for broad retraining and in-demand career funding retrieval, not exact occupation mapping. Do not confuse this applicant-focused program with the employer-focused Canada-Ontario Job Grant/Ontario Job Grant.

funding_amount: Covers tuition, compulsory fees, books, and other direct educational costs for eligible health human resources programs.
eligibility: Applicant must successfully apply to and enrol in an eligible program.
Applicant must be an Ontario resident.
Applicant must be a Canadian citizen, permanent resident, or protected person.
Applicant must commit to working in the same region where they studied after graduating.
Applicant must not be receiving funding from listed overlapping government programs such as Better Jobs Ontario.
notes: The official page lists eligible programs and regions, but not exact NOC codes. NOC mappings are intentionally left empty to avoid overclaiming.

funding_amount: For existing employees, government may cover 50% of eligible training costs up to $5,000 per employed trainee per fiscal year. For hiring and training an unemployed Albertan, government may cover up to 75% of eligible training costs up to $10,000 per trainee per fiscal year. Employer maximum is $100,000 per fiscal year.
eligibility: Employer must have current or potential employees who need training for current or future positions.
Eligible employers include private sector employers, non-profit sector employers, First Nations, and Metis Settlements.
Trainees must be current or prospective employees.
Trainees must be Canadian citizens, permanent residents, or protected persons entitled to work in Canada.
Ineligible trainees include company owners, family members, temporary foreign workers, and temporary workers in Canada.
notes: Employer-driven grant. Training must focus on productivity skills, be relevant to the trainee's job, be completed within 52 weeks, and be delivered in Alberta.

funding_amount: Up to $3,500 for eligible short-term skills training at public post-secondary institutions in British Columbia.
eligibility: Applicant must be living in British Columbia.
Applicant must be aged 19 or older.
Training must be an eligible short-term skills program at a public post-secondary institution.
A BC Services Card Account may be required for online application access.
notes: The official WorkBC page says the 2025/2026 program is currently closed for applications and points users to EducationPlannerBC for updates. Keep this caveat visible in user-facing output.

program_name: Workplace Innovation and Productivity Skills Incentive
funding_amount: May fund up to 75% of eligible training costs. Applicant funds the remaining balance.
eligibility: Applicant must be a legally registered business, industry association, sector council, or non-profit operating in Nova Scotia.
Applicant must have a direct workforce development need such as upskilling employees, adopting new technologies, or addressing critical skills gaps.
Applicant must demonstrate financial and administrative capacity to deliver the proposed initiative.
Applicant must operate within or support sectors aligned with Nova Scotia economic and workforce development priorities.
notes: Program prioritizes workforce development, innovation, productivity, critical skill shortages, and underrepresented groups. Current official page lists an intake period from April 1 to April 30, 2026.
